subject: Pioneer Health — sudden latency and 504s (KV prefetch contention?)
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Support <support@redwood.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-19T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: Spike in 504s + p99 latency — started ~10:12 PDT

Diego / Support team,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 504s and p99 latency for our tenant (tenant_id: pioneer-8891) beginning at ~10:12 PDT. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~6% in the last 5 minutes, and throughput dropped by ~40%. This is affecting our user-facing search flows.

Attached a quick perf snapshot and tail logs from our client side showing the 504s. Key observations from our team:
- Errors concentrated on the embeddings/generation route (v2-gen endpoint).
- Latency spikes correlate with a burst of small, repetitive requests (many short prefixes).

Can you confirm whether any config changes or maintenance are running in us-west? We need this remediated ASAP — happy to jump on a call.

Attachments: pioneer-perf-snapshot.png, pioneer-tail-logs.txt

Thanks,
Samir Khan
Senior SRE, Pioneer Health

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: support@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-19T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: Spike in 504s + p99 latency — Pioneer Health (tenant pioneer-8891)

Team — forwarding an urgent customer escalation from Pioneer Health. Key points: sudden jump in 504s and p99, tied to a burst of short-prefix traffic. Customer reports throughput collapse and ~6% error rate.

Immediate ask: please triage and implement short-term mitigation (see suggested list below). We should treat this as priority-high and loop in product/exec if needed.

Suggested immediate mitigations (short window):
- Limit prefetch concurrency for pioneer-8891 (reduce prefetch threads by 80% for this tenant).
- Enforce per-tenant KV cache occupancy caps (pin-prefix-ttl / lower max-keys).
- Temporarily disable aggressive prefix prefetch for generation endpoints for this tenant.
- If necessary, shift some traffic to a kept-warm model variant or route to dedicated lane.

I've attached the customer's logs. Jon — can you confirm whether this looks like a prefetch/eviction-induced HOL block? Laura/Marissa — would like to prep a short exec note once we have root-cause and mitigation timeline.

Diego
Support / Escalations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pioneer-tail-logs.txt (from customer)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-19T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Spike in 504s + p99 latency — Pioneer Health

Thanks for the ping, Diego. Quick triage notes (ops run just now):
- Observed large eviction spikes on hot shard(s) serving pioneer-8891 beginning 10:11 PDT; eviction rate shows repeated churn across short-lived prefix entries.
- Prefetch subsystem showed ~120 concurrent prefetch workers for that tenant; that's ~6x our typical per-tenant average and is thrashing the KV layer.
- Symptoms match head-of-line (HOL) blocking where hot shard write/evict activity is delaying reads and causing timeouts for other requests.

Immediate actions I will take now (applied at 10:36 PDT):
1) Reduce prefetch concurrency for tenant pioneer-8891 from 120 -> 24 (command: /ops/patch prefetch.concurrency pioneer-8891 24)
2) Enable tenant-specific cache occupancy cap: /ops/patch kv.max_keys.pioneer-8891 15000
3) Disable speculative prefetch for generation route: /ops/patch prefetch.speculative.enabled pioneer-8891 false
4) Open a guardrail to throttle burst QPS to 20% above baseline for 15 minutes if error rate remains > 2%

I've also linked the runbook (internal) for prefetched-thrashing mitigation: https://docs.redwood-internal/runbooks/prefetch-thrashing.

Next: monitor p99 and 5xx for 30 minutes; if no improvement we'll consider tenant isolation (move to dedicated lane) or fallback to a less aggressive model.

Jonas Weber
SRE — Platform

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-19T10:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Spike in 504s + p99 latency — Pioneer Health

Appreciate the fast triage. A couple of asks from CS/AM side:
- Customer is extremely sensitive to downtime; please provide ETA for visible mitigation so I can update the account team and support channel.
- Is credit/compensation likely? If short-term fix is <1hr we escalate status but hold off on credits; if longer we should prepare a goodwill credit.

Marissa — flagging for exec awareness. We may need to offer a single-digit % credit if impact persists beyond 60 minutes.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-19T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Spike in 504s + p99 latency — Pioneer Health

Thanks — approve the mitigations Jonas listed. Two requirements before broad rollout:
1) Ensure there's an automated rollback for each patch (preflight + post-metrics check).
2) Prepare a 1-page exec summary for Pioneer and our leadership with: impact window, hypothesis (prefetch-induced KV eviction/HOL), mitigation applied, monitoring status, and short-term next steps.

Diego — can you own the exec one-pager and customer-facing note? I want it in the thread in ~2 hours.

Marissa Cole
VP, Reliability Operations
Redwood Inference

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-19T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Spike in 504s + p99 latency — Pioneer Health

Update/exec one-pager (attached). Mitigations applied at 10:36 PDT (see Jonas' actions). Initial observations (10:50 PDT snapshot):
- p99 latency dropped from ~2.3s -> 0.9s for the generation route.
- 5xx rate reduced from 6% -> 0.7%.
- Throughput recovering to ~88% of baseline.

Immediate next steps (short term):
- Keep prefetch concurrency reduced for 30 minutes and evaluate.
- Run a targeted cache warmup for heavy prefixes to avoid eviction storms when we re-enable prefetch.
- Schedule post-incident cleanup: audit tenant prefetch patterns, recommend per-tenant prefetch caps in customer onboarding, and evaluate stronger tenant isolation heuristics.

Customer update draft (to send after we confirm stability for 30m):
"Samir — we've implemented an emergency mitigation that reduced error rates and latency. We're performing stabilizing steps now and will provide a full postmortem with permanent recommendations by EOD tomorrow. Apologies for the impact and thank you for the quick report"

Attachments: exec-one-pager.pdf

Diego Fernandez
Support / Escalations
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Khan <samir@pioneerhealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Pioneer Health — sudden latency and 504s (KV prefetch contention?)

Diego / team — thanks for the quick response. Error rate is back down to ~0.5% and user reports have improved. We'll keep a close eye on the next 24h and would like a postmortem that covers:
- Root cause analysis and whether tenant-specific prefetch caps are a permanent change.
- Any configuration changes that could avoid this for other tenants (we can share sample traffic patterns).
- Timing for a follow-up call (we're available tomorrow morning PT).

Appreciate the fast triage and the temporary mitigations.

Samir
Senior SRE, Pioneer Health
